key_insight: DiffVortex compresses the Biot–Savart kernel rather than the flow state, combining tensor-network acceleration with Lagrangian flexibility for moving and deforming bodies.
engineering_relevance: Its differentiable GPU implementation enables large-scale incompressible-flow simulations and gradient propagation through body–flow dynamics.
method: Evolve vorticity with Lagrangian vortex particles and model immersed bodies using bound vortex sheets.
Use quantics tensor cross interpolation to precompute tensor-network contractions for the fast multipole moment-to-local stage.
Prove that kernel QTT rank r yields convolution MPO rank at most 2^d r, independent of grid resolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 6.7×10^7 particles on one GPU, validation against cylinder and elliptical-vortex benchmarks, and demonstrations with rigid, multiple, and deforming bodies.
watch_item: Tensor-network efficiency depends on manageable kernel ranks; the abstract does not establish end-to-end logarithmic scaling or general three-dimensional performance.
paper_title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
